coupling.rationale: Server/client split is exemplary — one data seam, thin routes, prop-driven components — but the seam is untyped (any on both ends, no shared/ types), so payload changes surface as silent template breakage rather than compile errors.

app/app/components/MoveTables.vue:1 — moves tables are generic over per-method config (showLevel, sort keys)

app/app/pages/moves/[name].vue:1 — but the detail-page pattern (param → useFetch → NotFound → useHead) is copy-pasted in 4 pages (also pokemon/[name].vue:60, abilities/[name].vue:29, types/[name].vue:47)
app/app/pages/index.vue:26 — count + card-grid list markup duplicated in 4 pages (moves/[name].vue:38, abilities/[name].vue:13, types/[name].vue:29)

abstraction_design.rationale: The hard variations (cards, move tables, evolution trees) are well-designed and reusable, but the boilerplate around them — resource pages, card lists, species resolution — is copied rather than parameterized, so a similar-but-new case (Items) means mostly duplication.

findings.issue: All page-assembly functions return Promise<any> and every view consumes them via untyped useFetch, so the server→client payload contract is implicit and unverified
findings.suggestion: Define payload types in Nuxt 4's shared/ folder (or export them from server/utils) and type useFetch on the pages, so renaming a field fails at compile time

findings.issue: The 'resolve pokemon refs to species summaries, filter alternate forms, sort by dex id' loop is copy-pasted three times (also :448 and :484); a change to filtering/hidden rules needs three edits and each lookup is a linear scan of 1,025 species
findings.suggestion: Extract a resolveSpeciesSummaries(refs, {hiddenFlag}) helper that takes the index and returns sorted summaries once

findings.issue: The 'N Pokémon' count plus card-grid list markup is duplicated across four pages, so any list-wide feature (sorting, empty state, count wording) touches 4 templates plus 3 server sorts
findings.suggestion: Add a PokemonCardList component (props: species, showTypes) owning the count, ul and empty message

findings.issue: findSpeciesSummary is defined and exported but never called — dead code that misleads future edits
findings.suggestion: Delete it, or use it to deduplicate the three species-resolution loops

findings.issue: displayNumber/isMissing duplicated with app/app/pages/moves/[name].vue:55; dex-number padding duplicated between PokemonCard.vue:13 and pokeapi.ts:402
findings.suggestion: Move these small formatters to a shared composable/util (e.g. app/utils/format.ts, auto-imported in Nuxt)

findings.issue: getPokemonPage is a ~165-line monolith assembling stats, abilities, evolution and move tables inline
findings.suggestion: Extract the moves-table assembly (lines ~330-395) into its own module next to getMoveForTable

findings.issue: Detail-page boilerplate (route param → reactive useFetch → NotFoundPage if !found → computed useHead title) is copy-pasted in four pages; a fifth resource type copies it again
findings.suggestion: A small composable (useResourcePage(path, label)) would make new detail pages a few lines

findings.issue: All component styles live in one 600-line global stylesheet instead of scoped styles, so removing a component (e.g. PokemonCard) orphans its CSS blocks
findings.suggestion: Move per-component styles into scoped <style> blocks in the components; keep only tokens and layout in main.css

summary: This is a well-layered Nuxt 4 codebase with one clear data seam (server/utils/pokeapi.ts owns the API base, caching and all shaping) and genuinely reusable core components, so the hard variations — cards, move tables, evolution trees — are factored, not copied. The main editability risks are the completely untyped server→client payload contract and three-to-four-way duplication of the surrounding boilerplate (species resolution, card lists, detail-page scaffolding). I'd merge it with a note to extract a PokemonCardList and shared types before the next resource type is added.

scenarios.change: Change the API base URL and caching rules
scenarios.notes: One file owns everything: API_BASE (pokeapi.ts:4), apiGet (:79), mediaUrl (:60) and all five caches (rawCache, type/version-group/dex-index promises, preparedMoves); the client never knows the upstream. Difficulty drops one notch because the cache lives in five distinct ad-hoc mechanisms that must be reasoned about together, and API_BASE is captured at module load.
